title: Genre Template v1
description: A named binding of hard constraints, signed skills, and retrieval collections for one genre-and-style preset, within a single content form. Deliberately not a new first-class mechanism: every part of a template already has a home, and a template only names the combination. Templates are strategy, not instrument — they shape inputs and craft guidance, never acceptance criteria. See docs/ONLINE_POLICY_DESIGN.md for the one-way dependency they inherit.

genre.description: Same enum as eval-case-v1.json. Genre stays the evaluation quota and split axis; template is the product entry point. One genre may carry several templates.

differentiation_axis.description: What this template competes on. Required because the largest market lanes compete on beat density and emotional intensity, where this product's thesis — human credibility — is not the differentiator. A template that cannot state its axis is chasing volume in a lane with a sub-1% break-out rate.

market_note.description: Why this template exists commercially. Cite the observation, not a forecast.

constraints.description: Hard. Enforced at the admission gate, never scored.

forbidden_elements.description: Hard. The lazy resolutions this template refuses, checked deterministically at admission.

constraint_profiles.description: Versioned format/production profiles. Long and short episode-count variants share story-job/v1 and story-package/v1.

required_conditions.description: Semantic obligations assessed by the judge. Never an admission gate — the gate must stay deterministic.

skills.description: References into skills-registry/<name>/<semver>/, which only serves signed versions. Empty is legal and currently accurate: the registry holds nothing, so today a template binds constraints and retrieval only.

rubric_overrides.description: Locked to null, and the field is required so the lock is visible rather than merely absent. Per-template rubric weights would destroy cross-genre comparability: scores would become relative to a template, and 'does the revenge template do better than the family template' would stop having an answer. Templates change inputs and craft guidance; they never change acceptance criteria.

promoted_by_eval_run.description: Run id of the offline evaluation that promoted this template. Null means unpromoted and not permitted in production. A template is a candidate change exactly like a prompt or a weight.

content_form.description: Which content form this template lives inside. Only the scripted-drama form is defined today; knowledge/explainer and real-creator forms need their own artifact schema and rubric before they can appear here. A template is parameterisation WITHIN a form, never across forms.
